decisions.name: Almost Ramsey and Rowbottom residue
decisions.reason: The assigned design asks only for singularity and the consistency theorem.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Dimitriou, Chapter 2 §5, Lemmas 2.45–2.47 (printed p.71), concerns almost-Ramsey and Rowbottom residue in the symmetric model. The current page instead retains ordinary normal-measure Rowbottom homogeneity as lem-normal-measure-rowbottom-homogeneity and proves the Gitik singularity/consistency chain. These are different claims. The extra residue has no assigned consumer in the current manifest or SET-29/topology dependency interfaces; the exclusion stands.

decisions.name: PID implies no Suslin trees
decisions.reason: This result belongs to the separate Suslin-tree pair owned by batch 6 and is not used in either L/S-space proof.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Abraham, Three applications of ideal dichotomy, slides 5–6, explicitly discusses PID implies no Souslin trees. The named destination has order 687 and contains MA(aleph_1)-based elimination, not this PID implication. The PID definition and theorem lie on proper-forcing-countable-support-iterations-and-pfa at order 707, whose closure already requires the Suslin page. Moving this result to the recorded destination would require a forward dependency or reading-order decision. Owner must select a compatible destination; MA/PFA implies SH is not the same conditional theorem.

decisions.name: Other applications of Prikry forcing
decisions.reason: The assigned page stops at the standard preservation package and Gitik orientation.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Karagila §9.2 was read through Theorem 9.10, Lemmas 9.11–9.12, Proposition 9.13 (semiproper but not proper), and Exercise 9.14. The row names only unspecified other applications, and its reason says the page stops at Gitik orientation. The current page actually proves the Gitik class-forcing, symmetric-model, singularity and consistency chain. Owner must replace that stale boundary with an exact list of excluded applications; it cannot stand as written.

decisions.name: Tukey-order applications
decisions.reason: They are applications of the colouring not required for the assigned topology pair.

The current SET-29 inventory builds minimal walks, colouring, the L-space and the independent CH/PFA S-space branches. No selected consumer requires a Tukey classification, and none is being used in place of the retained oscillation lemma. Exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Diamond and infinite-power strengthenings
decisions.reason: The design asks for a CH S-space, not stronger hyperspace or infinite-power variants.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Hart–Kunen Ultra Strong S-Spaces introduction distinguishes CH strong S-spaces (all positive finite powers) from diamond-based ultra-strong function-space/infinite-power properties. The current page explicitly retains the CH finite-power theorem through thm-ch-implies-an-s-space-exists and does not assert the stronger diamond branch. SET-29 requires CH existence, not those additional function-space results. Exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Further PFA(S) consequences after Section 7
decisions.reason: These coherent-Suslin-tree preservation consequences are beyond the assigned direct PFA page and require a separate PFA(S) development.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Todorcevic Forcing with a coherent Souslin tree, introduction and later sections, studies the restricted PFA(S) axiom and forcing with S; it explicitly distinguishes this from PFA and its direct PID consequences. The current proper-forcing page retains full PFA, countable-support iteration and its direct topology/consistency consequences. No PFA(S) preservation development is selected. The additional consequences are correctly excluded.

decisions.name: Consistency proof for the dichotomy
decisions.reason: The prerequisite page owns the forcing-iteration and supercompact-to-PFA consistency theorem; this consumer proves its narrower omega_1-generated-ideal dichotomy locally from PFA.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: The named prerequisite page does contain cor-formal-consistency-of-pfa-from-a-supercompact and thm-pfa-implies-p-ideal-dichotomy, and the consumer independently proves its omega_1-generated simple-ideal dichotomy. However, this exact Abraham web source has an exhausted initial-plus-five recovery record and a documented source drop in batch-9 coverage. No complete cached version of those notes was recovered in this review; the separate applications slides do not supply their consistency proof. Owner-decision retains this precise source-verification limitation instead of claiming the declined source argument was read or equating the two dichotomies.

decisions.name: PID bounds the bounding number
decisions.reason: Not used in the assigned L/S-space chain.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Abraham applications slides 7–8 state PID implies b<=omega_2 and distinguish that bound from continuum bounds. Current no-S-space arguments use either the locally proved omega_1-generated ideal dichotomy or the preceding PFA/PID plus p>omega_1 branch. Neither is an appeal to the upper bound on b. The separate cardinal-invariant application is correctly excluded.

decisions.name: Small bases and finite-square discrete subspaces
decisions.reason: They go beyond the assigned existence/asymmetry claims and no selected destination owns them.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Moore Theorem 7.9 adds an uncountable discrete subspace in the square, and Theorem 7.13 gives the lower bound for a basis of uncountable regular Hausdorff spaces. The current L-space chain closes with the hereditary-Lindelof/nonseparability existence theorem and the CH/PFA asymmetry; it does not use these downstream refinements. Their exclusion preserves the assigned SET-29 contract.
